translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of Daxingshan Monastery, the Śramaṇa Mahāprajñā (Amoghavajra).
Translated by Imperial Decree by [Name]:

At that time, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara rose from his seat within the great assembly, prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground to pay homage at the Buddha’s feet, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"I have a mantra, a mudrā, and three messengers; the mantra is extensive."
For the sake of the benefit and peace of all good sons and good daughters in Jambudvīpa, I pray that you grant me permission to speak this method of great accomplishment.
May the World-Honored One, out of compassion, deign to hear it. The mantra is as follows:

*Rona-ni-mi-bha-ti svāhā.* Having recited this mantra, evil karma is extinguished.
If recited seven times, the five heinous crimes (*pañcānantarya*) are extinguished. If one reaches a full thousand recitations, there is no sin that will not be extinguished.
If one reaches a full hundred thousand recitations, one will see Avalokiteśvara face-to-face, adorned with all manner of ornaments, within seven days.
At the beginning of the ritual procedure, one may consume only milk-rice and ghee; on the final day, however, one must not eat.
On the fifteenth night, before the Buddha, one performs recitations without a fixed limit of number. When one sees the image shake and emit a voice crying out, "Excellent! Excellent!
and light shines forth, one should then place genuine jewels and precious objects upon the head of the mantra-practitioner; thus, wisdom is accomplished.
Having verified this by beholding Avalokiteśvara face-to-face, one shall fulfill all virtuous aspirations.
Furthermore, if one sees Avalokiteśvara adorned with various ornaments in a dream while drifting off to sleep, all wholesome deeds will be accomplished and all evil karma will be extinguished;
even those who simply recite this directly shall attain the eradication of their transgressions.
Next, it is taught that a single mudrā also benefits sentient beings. By performing this single mudrā thirty-two times, various things are accomplished.
Join the two hands together with the two thumbs placed back-to-back; press the two index fingers with the two thumbs to form hooks.
If this mudrā is directed toward the void, it serves as a celestial canopy for the realm; if directed toward the heavens in the ten directions, it establishes a boundary (sīmābandha) wherever one is.
Having performed the ritual for universal offering to the *iṣṭadevatā* and the universal prostration, one should subsequently perform the dedication of merit and the dismissal.
If one wishes to subjugate wicked persons, one should form the non-dual mudrā and recite [the mantra] one hundred and eight times with a mind of wrath;
thus all that is wrought by externalists shall be extinguished.
If a person suffers from a heart disease, empower yellow earth and apply it to the heart; they will be cured.
If a person suffers from a head disease, empower turmeric twenty-one times and ingest it; they will be healed.
If a person suffers from eye ailments, one should empower almond oil and apply it to cure the condition.
If a person suffers from swellings, one should empower fragrant powder one hundred and eight times and apply it to heal the affliction.
If one wishes to cause a person to depart far away, empower one hundred and eight pieces of bitter wood with mantras; that person will then depart.
Next, for the three seals of the messengers, the twenty-eight divisions are collectively subsumed: hold both palms flat toward the heavens and move the thumbs back and forth.
The celestial messenger Pukkasī, also known as Viśuddhā, has the secret mantra: *Pukkasīye hiḥ svāhā*.
With the two hands joined together, she comes and goes upon the two grounds.
The Great Sage Ākāśayakṣa, also known as Vasi, spoke in secret language:
"Sidyanta svāhā.
With both hands directed toward the sky, move the two thumbs back and forth.
The messengers of the lower realms—water, fire, and lightning—are also called Mahārāja.
Their secret mantra is: Oṃ jaḥye jaḥye svāhā.
These three types of messengers can extinguish the three calamities, extinguish the three kinds of attachments, and extinguish [the cycle of] birth after birth throughout all lifetimes.
Through these karmic obstacles, one shall achieve *siddhi* in every successive lifetime.
Furthermore, these three types of messengers do not contend with one another; they arise and perish instantaneously, turning the bowl, binding it, and joining wood to an empty bowl.

If a person attains the full power of the mantra, they may travel through the realm of space as an immortal (ṛṣi) and summon devas, nāgas, yakṣas, ghosts, spirits, and so forth, dispatching them at will;
this is especially due to the power of the dharma.

One fascicle of the *Āgama-mi-ichi-in-sen-rui-sen-ten-san-sha-ji-jōju-kyō-hō* (The Ritual Method for the Accomplishment of the Three Messengers, the Thousandfold Transformations of the Thousand Classes through the Single Seal of Āgama-mi).
On the sixth day of the seventh month in the fifth year of Jukan (1149), at approximately the hour of Shu,
it was respectfully received by the Vajra-disciple Ben-shin.
